explanation_types: The automatic classification of vertebral fractures has received much attention from the medical image analysis community.
However, because the solved task is classification at either vertebra or image level, the method still lacks interpretability and ease of clinical validation as other classification-based approaches.

On the other hand, patch-level predictions cannot be accurately mapped to individual vertebrae, giving only rough localization; thus only a single label per image can be predicted, which greatly reduces interpretability and potential for clinical validation.
A related problem is the interpretability of the methods' outputs.
